cascades_traced.name: Stripe webhook delivery — signature verification (per J-ADV-1 verified)
happy_path: 1. Stripe POSTs to /payment/stripe-webhook (bare) or /payment/stripe-webhook/{anything} (wildcard) per CsrfBareRouteException heal. Both paths excepted in VerifyCsrfToken::$except :32-35.
2. Route::post('/stripe-webhook/', [Stripe::class, 'handleWebhook']) registered in app/Http/PaymentGateways/Routes/stripe.php:26-28 with middleware chain ['installed', 'throttle:60,1'].
3. throttle:60,1 (60 req/min/IP) mitigates LAN HMAC-CPU DoS — verified by WebhookRouteHardeningTest:84-103 (61st hit = 429).
4. Stripe.php:199-208: config('services.stripe.webhook_secret') pulled, empty → response 500 misconfigured + Log::channel('fiscal')->error. No silent bypass.

5. Stripe.php:210-222: payload = $request->getContent() raw, $sigHeader = (string)$request->header('Stripe-Signature', ''). StripeClient\Webhook::constructEvent($payload, $sigHeader, $secret, 300) — explicit 300s replay tolerance (F-3 SYNC P1 V1.0.1 heal 2026-05-19, sentinel-locked by StripeWebhookReplayToleranceSentinelTest).
6. SignatureVerificationException → response 400 invalid_signature + Log::warning with IP. Stripe will not retry signature errors (per Stripe docs).
7. Throwable (payload parse) → response 400 invalid_payload + Log::error parse_error.
cascades_traced.verdict: VERIFIED — signature verify present, explicit 300s tolerance sentinel-locked, 400 on invalid sig + 500 on missing secret. J-ADV-1 attestation preserved.

cascades_traced.name: Cascade: payment.succeeded → Order update (PARTIAL — webhook does NOT mutate Order)
happy_path: 1. Stripe.php:284-310 inside DB::transaction: if ($eventType === 'charge.succeeded') extract charge.balance_transaction + charge.metadata.order_id (P0-POS-01 GOAL round-2 2026-05-18 — order_id injected into charges->create metadata at line 73).

2. CapturePaymentNotification::create(['order_id'=>$orderId, 'token'=>$balance_transaction, 'created_at'=>now()]) AFTER deleting any prior row for same order. Token bridges async webhook receipt to in-band success() controller.
3. $event->markProcessed($orderId) — WebhookEvent row flipped to STATUS_PROCESSED with order_id link.
4. Response 200 ok.

5. **HOWEVER** the webhook handler DOES NOT call PaymentService::payment(), DOES NOT mutate Order.payment_status, DOES NOT dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged. Cascade to POS Q10 / KDS is GATED on the user's browser hitting payment.success route (Stripe::success at :115-150) which then pops the CapturePaymentNotification token and calls PaymentService::payment() to flip Order.payment_status=PAID + create Transaction + (via OrderService changeStatus elsewhere) dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged.
6. There is NO cron/queue that drains stranded CapturePaymentNotification rows — they sit indefinitely until the user re-visits the success URL or admin/cashier manually intervenes.
cascades_traced.browser_death_scenario: User completes Stripe payment, Stripe charges card successfully, Stripe POSTs charge.succeeded webhook to backend → handler stages CapturePaymentNotification row + marks WebhookEvent processed. Browser dies / closes / loses network BEFORE Stripe redirect back to our payment.success route. Result: order stays in PaymentStatus::UNPAID (or its initial state). POS Q10 'à encaisser' panel never sees the order flip to PAID. KDS card never refreshes. Customer's card was charged but our system shows the order as unpaid. Cashier must reconcile manually.
cascades_traced.verdict: AMBER — webhook idempotency + staging correct, but cascade to Order.payment_status is browser-dependent. Webhook arrival alone does NOT complete the cascade. See K8-F-01 for full finding.

cascades_traced.name: Slow webhook — synchronous DB::transaction inside handler
evidence: Stripe.php:278-333 entire processing wrapped in DB::transaction() block + Throwable catch. Inner work: 1× DELETE on capture_payment_notifications + 1× INSERT capture_payment_notifications + 1× UPDATE webhook_events (markProcessed). On a healthy DB, p99 < 50ms.

NO heavy lifting (no broadcast dispatch, no FCM push, no audit_log HMAC chain write) inside the handler — those are deferred to the in-band success() controller path via the CapturePaymentNotification token (see K.8.3).
Stripe webhook timeout is documented at 30s (https://stripe.com/docs/webhooks#best-practices). Our handler comfortably fits in <100ms under normal load.

Risk window: if DB has lock contention (e.g. another worker holding row lock on webhook_events for a different stripe event_id — extremely unlikely with UNIQUE(provider, webhook_id) partitioned access pattern), or audit_log Cache::lock contention bleeds through (does NOT apply here, audit_log not written), or InnoDB innodb_lock_wait_timeout (capped at 5s per AppServiceProvider.php:233 GOAL-F2-HEAL-02) trips — handler returns 500 processing_failed → Stripe retries → DLQ row marked failed → hourly cron re-drives.
cascades_traced.verdict: MITIGATED — handler is fast by design (no heavy work inline). 5s DB lock timeout + 30s Stripe timeout = no retry-storm risk under realistic load. SAFE for V1 Le Cayenne traffic envelope.

cascades_traced.name: Large webhook payload — DoS vector per J-ADV-5
evidence: Stripe.php:210 $payload = $request->getContent() reads entire raw body into memory. NO application-level body-size cap (verified by grep on app/ and config/).

Defense layers OUTSIDE Laravel: nginx client_max_body_size (typically 1M default), PHP-FPM post_max_size (typically 8M default). Stripe's max event payload is ~64KB so realistic webhooks fit comfortably.
throttle:60,1 caps request rate per IP — combined with body-size caps at infra tier, multi-MB POST flood is bounded.

Signature verification happens AFTER full body read — a giant unsigned payload still consumes upload bandwidth + memory before being rejected at constructEvent. Stripe's HMAC scheme verifies the canonical 't={ts}.{payload}' so the full body is necessarily read.

Per J-ADV-5 prior finding: this is correctly classed as infra-tier risk, not application defect. V1.0.2 backlog: explicit Laravel max body filter (e.g. RouteServiceProvider middleware) if Le Cayenne nginx config is uncertain.
cascades_traced.verdict: INFRA-TIER (out of Laravel scope) — bounded by nginx + PHP-FPM body size + throttle:60,1. V1.0.2 backlog for explicit application-tier cap. See K8-F-05 (INFO).

cascades_traced.name: webhook_events PII retention — J-ADV-4 LEAK-04 P2 GDPR concern
evidence: Stripe.php:262 'payload' => $stripeEvent->toArray() stores the FULL provider event JSON for forensic audit. Grep on app/ for 'billing_details', 'redact', 'scrub' returns ZERO redaction logic on webhook_events.payload. PII protections elsewhere (KioskEventController, LoyaltyController, KDSOrderDetailsResource etc.) do NOT apply here.
No customer subject-access-request (SAR) tooling to surface webhook_events.payload rows when erasure is requested. Stripe webhooks are an under-the-radar PII reservoir.

cascades_traced.name: Webhook listener silent-fail risk per I.1 — MITIGATED
evidence: Stripe.php:319-333: inner DB::transaction wrapped in try/catch (Throwable). On error: Log::channel('fiscal')->error('stripe.webhook.processing_failed', [...]); $event->markFailed($e->getMessage()); response 500.
Stripe retries on 500 (per their docs). Failed WebhookEvent row stays in webhook_events with status=failed for hourly DLQ re-drive.

OutboxWebhookRetryFailedCommand.php:97-153 re-fetches failed rows within --since=24h window, ordered by id (deterministic tail on overflow), BATCH_CAP=500 per run. Writes audit_log 'outbox.replay' BEFORE dispatch (Wave 3 SYNC-ADV3-04 write-then-dispatch ordering), continues on individual event failure (preserves batch continuity).
Per CLAUDE.md outbox pattern: webhook → idempotency ledger persisted FIRST (firstOrCreate), then inner processing. Failure recovery via DLQ retry is guaranteed.
WebhookDLQRetryFailedTest validates the DLQ lane.

I.1 silent-fail concern: there is NO swallowed exception in the Stripe handler path. Every Throwable surfaces as 500 → Stripe retry → DLQ. The only swallow point is at the FAR DOWNSTREAM listener level (PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox catches DispatchDomainEventsJob::dispatch Throwable to avoid HTTP 5xx on broadcaster hiccup), but that listener is NEVER invoked from the Stripe webhook path because the webhook does NOT dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged (see K.8.3). So I.1 risk is materially zero for this surface.
cascades_traced.verdict: MITIGATED — try/catch + markFailed + 500 + Stripe retry + DLQ hourly. No silent-fail path exists. I.1 concern VERIFIED CLOSED for K.8 surface.

Runtime soft-guard EXISTS: Stripe.php:199-208 checks empty secret on every webhook POST and returns 500 misconfigured + Log::channel('fiscal')->error('stripe.webhook.misconfigured'). cascades_traced.verdict: AMBER — boot guard ABSENT (contradicts spec assumption), runtime soft-guard PRESENT (500 + Log::error on every miss). No silent NF525 violation possible. Promotion to boot-time guard recommended for parity with other secret-required configs. See K8-F-07.

findings.title: Webhook charge.succeeded does NOT flip Order.payment_status — stranded CapturePaymentNotification if user browser dies
findings.evidence: Stripe.php:284-310 only stages CapturePaymentNotification row + marks WebhookEvent processed. Order.payment_status flip to PAID happens in Stripe::success at :115-150 which is invoked ONLY when user's browser hits the payment.success route after Stripe's redirect. If browser dies (closed tab, dead phone, lost network) between Stripe charge capture and our redirect handler, the webhook fires successfully, CPN is staged, but no controller pops it. There is NO cron/queue that drains stranded CPN rows. NO fallback handler invokes PaymentService::payment from the webhook path.
findings.rationale: Webhook cascade is correctly idempotent + signature-verified but is structurally a stager, not a primary mutator. Real-world incidence: low (most browsers complete the redirect) but non-zero (mobile carrier latency / app backgrounding / tab close). When it happens: Stripe payout reconciliation diverges from our Z-report total. Customer charged but order shown unpaid. Cashier must reconcile manually after noticing.
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: Promote the webhook handler to flip Order.payment_status=PAID directly when charge.succeeded arrives with valid metadata.order_id (already injected since P0-POS-01 GOAL round-2 2026-05-18). Must wrap in DB::transaction with assertGatewayContext bypass (webhook IS a gateway context — extend PaymentAbstract or add a runtime allow flag). Must dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged to trigger the existing realtime cascade (PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox → DispatchDomainEventsJob → broadcast). Must use Order::whereKey + lockForUpdate to coexist safely with the in-band success() path (which also lockForUpdate). Plus: hourly cron to scan capture_payment_notifications older than 5min and consume them by calling success() programmatically.

findings.title: Webhook charge.failed has no cashier-facing notification
findings.evidence: Stripe.php:284 else-branch markProcessed() only. NO toast/email/push to cashier when a Stripe webhook says charge failed. The in-band Stripe::payment() :91-95 routes user to payment.fail when charges->create returns non-succeeded synchronously — so the live user gets a fail page. But webhook charge.failed arriving asynchronously (e.g. fraud check delayed) is silent on our side.
findings.rationale: In-band coverage is adequate for V1 single-restaurant + low Stripe volume. No NF525 risk (order stays UNPAID, no fiscal_sequence allocation). Webhook arrival is forensic-only.
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: If Stripe async failures become operationally relevant, add an Order.payment_status FAILED state (or a dedicated payment_failed_at timestamp) + cashier toast via OrderPaymentStatusChanged broadcast. V1 acceptable as-is.

findings.title: Webhook charge.refunded / refund.created (Stripe dashboard manual refund) does NOT flip Order.payment_status=REFUNDED
findings.evidence: Stripe.php:284 else-branch markProcessed() only — no RefundCreated::dispatch, no Order mutation. The full refund cascade (PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedOnRefundCreated → OrderPaymentStatusChanged outbox broadcast + stock release + loyalty clawback) is wired ONLY for in-app refunds (admin POS UI → RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute or PaymentService::cashBack).
findings.rationale: When owner refunds from Stripe dashboard (out-of-band), our Order.payment_status stays PAID. Stripe shows refunded. Z-report total no longer matches Stripe payout. NF525 fiscal sequence not invalidated (correctly) but ledger divergence breaks reconciliation. Stock not released, loyalty points not clawed back, POS/admin/OSS show stale PAID until manual fix.
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: Handle charge.refunded (and charge.refund.updated for partial refunds) by extracting metadata.order_id, locking the Order, and dispatching RefundCreated via a thin gateway-context wrapper. Since RefundCreated already exists with the full downstream cascade hardened (WG-1-WF6-P1-1 + GOAL-J2-HEAL-07 loyalty isolation), the lift is minimal. For partial refunds, need to extend PaymentStateMachine + Order schema (payment_status enum currently REFUNDED is all-or-nothing). Recommend: V1 operations doc instructs owner to refund FROM POS UI only, never Stripe dashboard, until V1.0.2 cascade lands.

findings.title: Webhook charge.dispute.created / chargeback has no owner notification or Order tagging
findings.evidence: Stripe.php:284 else-branch markProcessed() only. No PaymentStatus::DISPUTED enum value. No email/push to owner. No audit_logs row 'order.dispute_created'. Owner relies on Stripe dashboard email alone.
findings.rationale: V1 Le Cayenne single-restaurant + owner sees Stripe email + dashboard daily → operationally acceptable. 180d webhook_events retention preserves forensic for the PCI dispute window. NF525 chain unaffected (order was correctly PAID at the time; dispute is a downstream banking event).
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: For SaaS multi-tenant or owner-staff separation: add PaymentStatus::DISPUTED + audit_logs entry + push notification + admin dashboard dispute pill. Schema for dispute amounts, win/lose outcome, evidence-due-date. Out of V1 scope per CLAUDE.md §15 V1 focus directive.

findings.title: Large webhook payload — no Laravel-level body cap, mitigated at nginx/PHP-FPM tier
findings.evidence: Stripe.php:210 $request->getContent() reads full body. Grep on app/ + config/ returns no application-tier max body filter. Defense at infra: nginx client_max_body_size + PHP-FPM post_max_size + Stripe events realistically <64KB + throttle:60,1.
findings.rationale: Per J-ADV-5: infra-tier classification, not application defect. V1 Le Cayenne nginx config likely default 1M cap — Stripe webhooks fit comfortably. Multi-MB POST flood bounded by rate-limit + body cap. Signature verification reads full body before reject (required by Stripe HMAC scheme), so attacker can burn 1M × 60 RPM upload bandwidth per IP — acceptable.
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: Document explicit nginx + PHP-FPM body caps in CRONTAB_PROD.md / runbooks. Optionally add Laravel middleware enforcing ≤128KB on /payment/*-webhook/* paths for application-tier defense-in-depth.

findings.title: webhook_events.payload stores Stripe billing_details (name, email, phone, address) for 180d unredacted — GDPR Article 5(1)(c) data minimization gap
findings.evidence: Stripe.php:262 'payload' => $stripeEvent->toArray() captures full provider payload. Stripe charge objects routinely embed billing_details: { name, email, phone, address }. PruneWebhookEventsCommand:31-38 retains processed/duplicate 180d (PCI dispute window). Failed rows NEVER pruned (DLQ retry lane). No redaction logic exists (grep on app/ for billing_details/redact/scrub).
findings.rationale: GDPR data minimization principle: operational need is event metadata (id, type, amount, currency, order_id) — billing_details exceeds the minimum. Subject access request (SAR) tooling does not currently surface webhook_events rows. 180d is defensible for PCI dispute lookback but not necessarily for PII.
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: Add a scrubBillingDetails($payload) helper invoked at firstOrCreate insert time. Whitelist allowed keys (id, type, amount, currency, balance_transaction, metadata, status, livemode, created). For partial payments / failed events, scrub at write-time to remove name/email/phone/address.line1-2/postal_code. Add SAR query helper that scans webhook_events.payload->>'$.billing_details.email' for erasure-request matches. Backfill migration to scrub existing rows beyond N days (defaulting 30d for tighter retention).

findings.title: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET not in AppServiceProvider production boot guard list — runtime soft-guard only
findings.evidence: AppServiceProvider.php:78-223 verified guard list: POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE / payment.bypass / printing.bypass / APP_DEBUG / idempotency.enabled / LOYALTY_QR_SECRET / APP_URL / broadcasting.default / queue.default / cache.default. STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent. App boots cleanly in production even with empty STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Runtime soft-guard present at Stripe.php:199-208 (per-request 500 misconfigured + Log::error).
findings.rationale: Task spec asserted 'app refuses to boot if missing in production' — this assumption is FALSE. There is NO boot refusal. There IS a per-webhook-receipt runtime refusal which prevents silent signature-verify bypass (handler never proceeds to constructEvent without a secret). Operational delta: deploy-with-missing-secret discovered at first webhook receipt (seconds) vs boot (instant) — not a silent corruption. Stripe will retry 500 ~10× over ~3 days, filling fiscal log with 'stripe_webhook_secret_missing' until secret is set + config:cache run.
findings.v102_backlog_suggestion: Promote STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET to boot-time guard in AppServiceProvider.php at line ~190 (between APP_URL and broadcasting.default — same defensive band). Pattern: if (empty(config('services.stripe.webhook_secret', ''))) throw new RuntimeException('STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET must be set in production. ...'). Optional: scope to only-when-Stripe-gateway-enabled (PaymentGateway::where(slug=stripe, status=ENABLE)->exists()) to avoid hard-failing deployments that don't use Stripe at all. Mirror LOYALTY_QR_SECRET pattern at line 161-171.

top_3_cascade_concerns: 1. P1 K8-F-01: Webhook charge.succeeded does NOT flip Order.payment_status — full cascade gated on user browser visiting payment.success. Browser-death window leaves stranded CapturePaymentNotification + Stripe-charged-but-order-UNPAID state. No drain cron. POS Q10 panel never refreshes. Mitigation: V1.0.2 promote webhook to direct PAID flip + dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged.

2. P1 K8-F-03: Webhook charge.refunded (Stripe dashboard manual refund) does NOT trigger RefundCreated cascade — Order ledger diverges from Stripe ledger, Z-report total mismatch, stock not released, loyalty not clawed back, no realtime broadcast. V1 operational mitigation: instruct owner to refund FROM POS UI only. V1.0.2 wire charge.refunded → RefundCreated bridge.

3. P2 K8-F-06 (GDPR) + K8-F-07 (boot guard) + K8-F-04 (dispute UX): three independent V1.0.2 backlog items. None block V1 ship. Boot-guard promotion is the cheapest fix (~10 lines). PII scrub requires schema/audit thinking. Dispute UX requires PaymentStatus enum extension.
